A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LintSeq research. The main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices are readable and sufficiently complete to match retained, revised, relocated, and removed material.

before.justification: v1 reports original TinyCodeLM pretraining and fine-tuning results, HumanEval and MBPP(+) evaluations, linter ablations, and synthetic-data analyses.

after.justification: v3 reports original model evaluations and ablations, including additional results on CodeContests, DS-1000, and BigCodeBench Instruct.

M1.justification: Both versions use random line deletion with iterative linter cleanup, reverse the resulting program states into insertion-only diffs, and train models with teacher-forced supervision. Architectures and edit-resolution procedures are retained. v3 adds pseudocode and revises the stated linter guarantee without specifying a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: v3 extends evaluation beyond HumanEval and MBPP(+) to competitive programming through CodeContests, data-science completion through DS-1000, and complex instruction/function-call tasks through BigCodeBench Instruct. These substantially broaden evaluated task requirements. Training corpora and Python-only experimental coverage remain unchanged.

E2.justification: v3 removes the Figure 1 comparisons with GPT-4, GPT-4-Omni, Llama 3.1 405B, and Nemotron-4 340B, substantially narrowing external comparison scope. PolyCoder's 160M and 400M rows disappear from the tiny-model comparison. Standard Instruct rows also disappear from the corresponding TinyCodeLM high-sampling tables, although baseline comparisons remain elsewhere. RandSeq is retained.

E3.justification: The principal HumanEval/MBPP scaling evaluations change from 50 completions at temperature 1 and top-p 0.95 to 64 completions with temperature, top-p, and min-p sweeps. New protocols include 128 completions for CodeContests, 40-completion DS-1000 evaluation, and greedy BigCodeBench decoding. The lint-error audit also changes top-p to 1. These are substantive evaluation changes, not evidence of changed training.

E4.justification: v3 revises the existing linter-ablation and error-frequency studies under new sampling settings, emphasizing pass@1 in the main text while retaining higher-pass ablation results in Appendix A.2. The pretraining-progress analyses in v1 Figures 12-13 are removed. The sequence-count sensitivity analysis in Figure 11 is retained unchanged.

E5.justification: v1 mainly presents point estimates, aggregate plus/minus summaries, and unlabeled uncertainty bars in its error-frequency plot. v3 explicitly reports standard errors for individual scores in Table 1 and Tables 2-6, adds standard-error bands for fitted compute-scaling curves, and asserts statistical significance for linter ablations. No increase in independent training runs or seeds is documented.

E6.justification: v3 adds complete results for three harder benchmarks and replaces many HumanEval/MBPP results under revised sampling conditions; these differences are not same-setting performance gains. In the retained temperature-tuned tiny-model comparison, baseline 400M HumanEval pass@1 changes from 9.6 to 11.3, and baseline 150M MBPP(+) pass@10 changes from 16.4 to 21.6. v3 also contains a discrepancy: Section 3.4 gives 14.2 for 400M LintSeq MBPP pass@1, while Table 3 and Figure 5 give 14.7.

T1.justification: v1 describes intermediate states as producing no linter errors. v3 Sections 2.1 and 2.4 instead define linter-error-free states by matching the original program's error traces and explicitly define order-preserving subsets of program lines. Appendix B.1 also removes v1's specific 16L token-overhead expression. The edit-sequence mathematics and FLOP approximation otherwise remain equivalent; no new proof is introduced.

C1.justification: v3 removes the headline claim of GPT-4-competitive coverage at comparable inference cost and narrows tiny-model state-of-the-art claims to competitive performance. Its abstract, introduction, and conclusion instead emphasize preserved or improved pass@1 and stronger scaling with total test-time FLOPs across broader tasks. This materially changes the scope and strength of the advertised contributions.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly distinguishes linters from formal verifiers and discusses missed errors. It removes v1's speculative explanation attributing Phi-3 pass@1 weaknesses to prior instruction tuning and distribution shift. The retained insertion-only limitation gains proposed remedies using human edit data or reinforcement learning, and the discussion adds instruction-tuning versus pretraining scope. The central diversity interpretation remains.

D1.justification: v1 promises a future code release; v3 provides code/model access information and a reproducibility statement describing implementation and experiment scripts, whose availability is not independently verified here. Most training details are retained. v3 removes the per-model token-count table supporting FLOP calculations and adds a generic maximum learning rate of 1e-4 that conflicts with its retained model-specific peak rates.

R1.justification: The closest-prior-work discussion expands substantially to edit representations, Levenshtein Transformer, code sketches, TFix, and Can It Edit?, beyond v1's emphasis on commit-based instruction tuning. The introduction also replaces the broad absence-of-edit-data argument with a more specific gap concerning sequential coverage and edit granularity. New benchmark references support the expanded evaluation.

P1.justification: The abstract, introductory motivation and contribution list, experimental narrative, and conclusion undergo substantial rewriting. v3 adds a Definitions subsection and reproducibility statement, reorganizes evaluation explanations, and moves Additional Results from the final appendix to Appendix A. These changes substantially alter the narrative and document organization beyond added experiments.

P2.justification: Figure 1's external-model comparison is replaced by paired compute-scaling plots, Figure 2 is redrawn with pseudocode, and experimental displays are reorganized into bar charts and FLOP-based curves. The two tiny-model comparison tables are merged, and the lint-error display becomes an error-free-percentage chart. Dataset statistics move to the appendix; retained examples and sensitivity plots are relocated, while pretraining plots are removed.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens the central empirical case beyond v1's two-benchmark, largely fixed-decoding evaluation: harder task coverage, decoding sweeps for both variants, paired FLOP-based comparisons, and explicit uncertainty better support generality and efficiency claims. It also moderates the GPT-4 and tiny-model superiority claims. These gains outweigh lost pretraining/token-count detail and localized reporting inconsistencies, including the Section 3.4/Table 3 discrepancy and conflicting learning-rate entries.
